title: What is 6 ÷ 0, really?
hook: 6 ÷ 2 is 3 because three 2s make 6. Ask the same question about 0.

knows: division asks "how many of these make that"
doesNotKnow: why 6 ÷ 0 has no answer, rather than being 0 or "infinity"

misconception: 6 ÷ 0 = 0 (dividing by nothing leaves nothing), or it is a very large number called infinity.
objective: The learner can explain that 6 ÷ 0 is undefined because no number times 0 gives 6, and that shrinking scoops need more and more of them with no single limit.

claims.text: Scoops of 3, 1 and 0.1 fill 6 in 2, 6 and 60 scoops: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, 6 ÷ 1 = 6, 6 ÷ 0.1 = 60.
claims.source: Arithmetic; company/domains/briefs/checks/math-wave-j-check.mjs label A3 (3 2, 1 6, 0.1 60). The reveal names only the sizes the learner poured, recorded when they pour.
claims.note: Arithmetic: 6/3 = 2, 6/1 = 6, 6/0.1 = 60. JavaScript gives 59.999..., but count() rounds to 60 and the jug draws 60 bands.

claims.text: 6 ÷ a scoop size asks how many scoops fill the jug: a ÷ b is the number q with q × b = a.
claims.source: Definition of division as the inverse of multiplication (the measurement, 'how many fit', reading).
claims.note: Definition: a / b is the q with q x b = a (the measurement reading of division).

claims.text: Any number times 0 is 0 (6 × 0, 1,000 × 0 and 1,000,000 × 0 are all 0), never 6, so no number q passes the check q × 0 = 6, and 6 ÷ 0 has no answer: it is left undefined. A scoop of 0 poured 1,000 times fills 0 of 6.
claims.source: q × 0 = 0 for every q (check A3, zero [0, 0, 0, 0]); 1,000 × 0 = 0.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal now ties 'undefined' to the check (learner r10); previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Derivation: q x 0 = 0 for every q, so no q solves q x 0 = 6, and 6/0 is undefined in the real numbers. Recall (5/0) checks out. Scope note: the claim is about ordinary (real-number) arithmetic. Some extended systems (the projective real line) write 6/0 = infinity, but there infinity is not a number that times 0 gives 6, so 'No number works' stands. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Derivation: q x 0 = 0 for every q; CHECKS = [6, 1000, 1000000] each shown as '... × 0 = 0'; ZERO_TRIES = 1000 pours of a 0 scoop fill 0. No q satisfies q x 0 = 6, so 6 ÷ 0 is undefined in ordinary arithmetic. The new reveal ties 'undefined' to the check ('No number passes the check, so 6 ÷ 0 has no answer: it is left undefined').

claims.text: As the scoop size shrinks toward 0, 6 ÷ size grows with no ceiling: the climb never lands on a count, so no huge number is the answer, and infinity is not one either (infinity scoops of nothing would still hold nothing: a scoop of 0 adds 0 however many times it is poured).
claims.source: 6 ÷ s > N whenever 0 < s < 6/N, so 6 ÷ s is unbounded as s → 0 and has no limit; and q × 0 = 0 ≠ 6 for every huge q. Standard: infinity is not a real number, and the one-sided limits of 6/x as x -> 0 are +infinity and -infinity, so even the limit does not exist (builder's note; no source opened).
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal now answers the 'infinity' chooser (learner r10); previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Derivation: 6/s > N whenever 0 < s < 6/N, so 6/s is unbounded as s -> 0+, and no real q satisfies q x 0 = 6. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Derivation: 6/s > N whenever 0 < s < 6/N, so 6/s is unbounded as s -> 0+; no finite count is reached. 'Infinity scoops of nothing would still hold nothing' restates q x 0 = 0 for the 'infinity' chooser; it does not assert an extended-real arithmetic. Reveal text (Demo.tsx lines 58-60) matches.

recall.question: A calculator shows an error for 5 ÷ 0. Why?
options: The answer is too big to show
The answer is 0, shown as an error
recall.why: 5 ÷ 0 would be the number q with q × 0 = 5, but every number times 0 is 0. No number works, so it is undefined, not huge and not 0.
